newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg says eyeing possible expansion.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg says eyeing possible expansion.

text.p: Swedish metals and mining company Trelleborg AB said on Thursday all its units were considering acquisitions and joint ventures but that it had no comment on market rumours.
"The Trelleborg group is in an important development phase which will give the group a partially new structure in time," Trelleborg said in a statement.
"Discussions are ongoing within all groups just now concerning acquisitions and various joint venture projects," it added.
Trelleborg shares jumped seven percent in early trade Thursday on a newspaper report on Thursday it was planning to spin off its mining and metals unit Boliden, listing it on the Stockholm bourse.
At 1455 GMT the share traded at 106 crowns, up nine.
The company said that its rubber products unit was prioritising increased volumes and that this was evident considering acquisitions in recent years.

Within its distribution unit, intensive negotiations were taking place with several possible partners. Its mining and metals unit was in talks about potential links and its goal was increased internationalism.

"As for Mines & Metals, discussions are taking place with a series of interested parties which represent a broad spectrum of business and cooperation forms, where increased internationalism is a key goal," Trelleborg said.
The company said it was not surprising that the market was buzzing with rumours but repeated that it had no comment on the rumours.
"With such high activity and so many ongoing discussions, some rumours could emerge. When there is substantial information about developments within an area, Trelleborg will announce it," it added.
